answer: Coordination Density Pricing. Each identity accrues a periodic fee proportional to the number of distinct counterparties it transacts with in a window, tracked by pair counters. An attacker running many identities must pay the sum of pairwise densities, which grows with fan-out; a single identity in a dune of activity costs more than a quiet meadow account. A raven flag halts accounts whose counterparty entropy spikes faster than settlement volume. The attacker's per-identity cost rises with coordination breadth, not count alone.
